# librevna

**The PC program for the LibreVNA, an open-hardware 6 GHz vector network analyser**

- **Version recorded:** 1.6.5
- **Categories:** `antenna-analysers`, `electronics`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/jankae/LibreVNA>

## What it does

LibreVNA-GUI is the program that drives a LibreVNA, the open-hardware two-port vector network analyser (100 kHz to 6 GHz), over USB. It sweeps the device and shows the results on Smith, polar and XY charts with markers and math on the traces; it calibrates against a calibration kit, de-embeds fixtures, transforms to the time domain to find faults along a cable (TDR), and saves Touchstone files. It also runs the device as a spectrum analyser and as a signal generator, and it can update the device's firmware. A SCPI server lets other programs and scripts drive it over TCP.
**The device emits RF from its ports.** Sweeping is the device sending a signal out of a port into whatever is connected -- usually an antenna, a filter or a cable under test -- and the generator mode sends a steady carrier. An antenna on a port radiates that signal. Installing the program sends nothing; the device emits only while it sweeps or generates.

## Why you would want it

The catalog's `nanovna-saver` and `flaa` speak to the NanoVNA and to RigExpert analysers; nothing spoke to the LibreVNA, an open design with two full ports, whose program upstream publishes for Linux as source and as a zip of a prebuilt binary. This is that program built from its tagged source.

## Before it will work

A LibreVNA, and access to its raw USB device: see the `librevna` hardware entry, whose identifiers are read from upstream's source and not yet seen on hardware here, so no udev rule is generated from it yet. A calibration kit for the connector type you measure through, and the time to calibrate before measuring.

## Known problems

**Its SCPI server listens on every network address by default.** Upstream's preferences enable it on TCP port 19542, and `tcpserver.cpp` listens on `QHostAddress::Any`, with no password: on a network, any machine that can reach the laptop can drive the instrument, including its generator. Turn it off under Preferences when you do not need it, or firewall the port. The streaming servers (ports 19000 to 19101) are off by default.
What was measured: built on Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and Kali, and started under a virtual display with no device on all three: it opened its four-trace VNA window with "No device connected", logged "Listening on port 19542", and on Ubuntu 24.04 and Kali the container's /proc/net/tcp6 showed that port bound to every address. Not measured: a LibreVNA, calibration, a sweep, the generator, a firmware update, or SCPI from another program.

## Keeping it current

- probe: github tags (`jankae/LibreVNA`)
- strategy: rebuild
- Upstream tags about once or twice a year (v1.6.2 2025-02, v1.6.3 and v1.6.4 2025-05, v1.6.5 2026-03) and keeps fixing on master between them. Move the tag and its commit together, and check the device entry's identifiers against librevnausbdriver.cpp at the new tag.
